title: A secular evection model permits large tidal-depth changes for two ASASSN-14ko companion fits
abstract: We test whether relativistic precession can act in resonance with two proposed circular companions of ASASSN-14ko. We derive and check a planar model that averages over the stellar orbit but retains the companion phase. At an active black-hole mass of 10 million solar masses, stable evection centres occur at stellar eccentricities 0.96852 and 0.93319. The formal resonance domains overlap the nominal eccentricity 0.9 used in prior orbit tests for some apsidal phases. A long-period example changes pericentre by a factor of 2.228 in 19 observer years. A short-period example reaches a 20-gravitational-radius model cut in 3.221 years; its later path is unresolved. The resonance centres also give a stellar-radius test if tidal penetration is near one. Averaging over the companion phase removes this effect. The result is conditional on a circular companion, coplanar prograde motion, a quadrupole tide and leading Schwarzschild precession. It does not detect a companion, validate the secular approximation against full dynamics, fit observed epochs or explain a stalled orbital period. We provide code, model tracks, independent potential and torque checks, source hashes and figures.

display.caption: Formal secular resonance centres and boundaries for two conditional companion fits. High-eccentricity parts can exceed the weak-field model domain.
Six model tracks with fixed secular semimajor axis. The short solid track stops at a 20-gravitational-radius validity cut.
